An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time has been made by researchers using approximately 37 inverse picobarns of LHCb data. This calculation took into account various $B^0_s$ production and decay modes taking place at or just above their threshold, specifically $p=1.8$ TeV, along with proton beams colliding head-on. By comparing sidebands to signal regions around $M_{KK} = 1949-2011$ MeV, the team applied several constraints to minimize $B^0_s\rightarrow \phi\phi$ and $B^0_s\rightarrow \rho^+\rho^-$ influences. The average $B^0_s$ decay time in this range emerged as $0.154 \pm 0.022$ ps, with a precision of 14.5%.

This research paper focuses on the numerical solutions to a distributed control problem governed by a stochastic evolution equation, specifically the objective of bringing a dynamic system under constraints to rest using optimal control. We develop a mathematical model, derive a corresponding discrete-time model, and demonstrate the existence and a unique solution for the discrete-time problem. Furthermore, we establish the convergence of the discrete solutions to the continuous solutions in a stochastic sense. A computational method using Lagrange multipliers along with the Euler method and the Euler scheme for a stochastic optimal control problem is employed to find the numerical solutions.

Our investigation into the directional properties of extremely high-energy cosmic rays revealed that their distribution extends far beyond the Megalanic Cloud region and the Fornaci Wall. Within the scope of our observations, we focused on the most distant areas and analyzed the patterns of these cosmic rays in the southern celestial sphere. Our data showed that the distribution of these cosmic rays takes the shape of two large clusters that differ in intensity, with the most distant cluster being over 12 degrees in diameter. We found that the distribution of cosmic rays in this most distant area can be accurately described using a multi-source anisotropy model, with the remaining component being randomly distributed. Based on our observations, we estimated the number of distant cosmic sources to be anywhere from 20 to over a hundred, with the energy output of these sources being in the order of 10 to the power of 51 Watts. We also examined the distribution of cosmic rays in the northern celestial sphere and the connection between the two hemispheres, with our findings consistent across different energy ranges.

This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses the characteristic of being solvable, thus extending and building upon previous work by Benayadi and the first author.

Our research identified variations in flow angles and flow magnitudes relative to the collision plane in high-energy nucleus-nucleus collisions. Using data from the ALICE experiment at the LHM, specifically in lead-lead collisions at a 5.02 TeV energy level, we determined the angle of the second-harmonic flow relative to the collision plane and found it to be 4.44 radians on average. Furthermore, we compared this value to theoretical predictions made within the iEBE-VISHNU model and other models such as MUSIC and AMPT, and discussed the implications of our findings for theoretical models of the quark-gluon plasma state encountered in these high-energy collisions.

We introduce a new framework where data tables with entries containing unknown values can be enhanced with additional rules, known as superdependencies. We investigate the properties of these advanced rules, exploring their behavior under union, intersection, and aggregation operations. Furthermore, we examine ways to handle inconsistent data in problem-solving applications that utilize expert systems. A key aspect of our analysis is comparing superdependencies to existing concepts like datalog regulations and data exchange relationships. We also tackle the challenge of repairing tables containing entries with unknown values, starting from a set of specified superdependencies. This process yields a minimal repair that is consistent with the data and the rules, and we provide a data-driven algorithm to compute this repair.

We introduce a novel dynamic model, the Poisson autoregressive process of order Q with time-varying parameters, denoted as PARQtv. This model builds on the traditional positive autoregressive process of order Q, with a key distinction being the time-dependent nature of PARQtv parameters. We prove the existence and uniqueness of the stationary distribution for the PARQtv process and derive an explicit formula for the conditional mean parameters that drive the model's evolution. Furthermore, we establish the strong consistency of the maximum likelihood estimator for the PARQtv process. To evaluate the performance of PARQtv, we conduct a simulation study and analyze a real-world data set consisting of football goal statistics.

Our novel object representation model, Neural Descriptor Fields (NDF), generates object representations that are invariant to rotations, translations, and scaling. This model, inspired by Baxter's work using neural networks with bounding box annotations, leverages object descriptors aligned with their spatial context. In contrast to methods that rely on orientation-aware representations or extensive 3D point cloud data, NDF uses only 2D images. Through thorough experimentation on VOC and KITTI datasets, our findings demonstrate significant enhancements over current state-of-the-art methods.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. For all values of Q, including those less than 2, we have determined the precise equations of the critical fixed point relevant to Q ≤ 2, especially within the mean-field approximation where it is equal to 2. Our findings confirm that the dimensionless ratio rQ = xQ / r c Q remains a critical parameter, determining the singularity's position through a combination of r Q and Q. Our data show that near the Q = 2 threshold, the ratio r c Q gradually decreases, taking on values of 2.52, 1.40, and 0.80 for Q = 2, Q = 3/2, and Q = 4/3 respectively. Furthermore, our results within the mean-field approximation where r c Q = 2 are consistent with previous research using perturbation theory and the ɛ-expansion.

In statistics and physics, when analyzing a random TAP reconstruction on the ground state of a random Ising model, a key result shows that there's a curve that represents the expected TAP free energy for all nearby states. This result was initially proven by on. In a new approach, researchers have demonstrated that this expected TAP free energy is curved for all nearby states by applying a variation of the Sudakov-Fernique concentration inequality.

While using photometry from stars in the sky to measure the atmosphere's aerosol properties has been an interesting idea for decades, it not until recently this concept has been put into practical use. Historically, scientists relied on theoretical models to explore this method's potential, but now we are seeing the emergence of actual applications. A team used data from the CALET RBX on board the ISS to measure the atmosphere's aerosol characteristics over Africa, and another group used data from the TESS space telescope to study the aerosol properties in the Indian Ocean and over India, and in another study they examined aerosol properties in desert regions and over the Amazon rainforest.

Our proposed method, DeepHMap++, tackles the 2D pose estimation from depth images with multiple objects by leveraging the benefits of both projection clustering and correspondence learning. We introduce an initial framework called the pose proposal network (PPN) that generates an initial set of 2D pose proposals through clustering based on projection clustering, and a refiner called the correspondence refinement network (CRN) that refines these proposals by finding the corresponding points on the ground truth mask. We improve the original projection clustering framework by incorporating a spatial-aware adjacency graph that captures the structural relationships between pose proposals, and demonstrate the efficacy of our method by achieving superior results on the NYUDv2 dataset for the single-greatest DoF pose estimation task, and comparable performance to leading methods on the SUN3D dataset for the multi-greatest DoF pose estimation task.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. The package tackles sparse inverse problems on graphs, recovering an
estimator for the inverse matrix based on observed data and sparsity constraints
imposed on its off-diagonal elements. We demonstrate the versatility of GGLasso
by applying it to various problems, including sparse representation, selection,
estimation, and recovery of latent variables in graphical models and CCA models.

Due to the extensive dimensionality of configurational spaces, molecular systems exhibit a high degree of freedom, leading to an extremely large number of possible configurations. As a result, it is essential to utilize an efficient and robust framework for exploring and sampling configurational spaces effectively. Our study presents an optimized method for configurational sampling through the application of Langevin dynamics, combined with our novel Neighbor-List Junction Barrier (NLJB) technique. By leveraging the beneficial properties of junction barriers in conjunction with a neighbor list, we are able to achieve a significant boost in the equilibrium configurational sampling rate by at least two orders of magnitude compared to traditional methods, following the prediction made by Lubenski et al. Our findings are further validated through the computationally demanding simulation of a polyisoprene chain, resulting in an accurate reproduction of its known properties.

Our proposed method enhances eigenvector centrality within multilayer networks by taking into account the level of reliance between different layers, allowing for the calculation of comprehensive node rankings that accurately reflect across-layer connectivity. This enhancement is particularly useful for detecting across-layer influential individuals, as research has shown it accurately identifies the most reliant nodes that connect different layers of a network. Furthermore, our proposed approach is capable of accounting for variations in node importance within individual network layers. In contrast, traditional eigenvector centrality measures node importance based on overall network connectivity. We demonstrated the effectiveness of this method using synthetic data and real-world examples, including academic collaboration networks and social media data.

Recently, we generated a new quantum field theory framework known as $R$-quantum field theory, which integrates the concept of $q$-deformed quantum field theory and $k$-deformed quantum field theory. This new framework allows for the investigation of quantum field theory within the Fock space, even in the presence of Lorentzian geometry changes. In this study, we establish a new representation of the Dirac matrix within the $R$-Minkowski space-time framework, which is analogous to the original representation. Notably, we demonstrate that the Dirac equation remains unchanged in the $R$-Minkowski space-time, even when the Lorentzian metric components undergo arbitrary alterations, as long as the metric remains pseudo-Euclidean.

This study investigates how surface tension affects spheres as they enter water at moderate speeds, a phenomenon previously misunderstood due to limited research in this specific speed range. High-speed cameras were used to capture and analyze multiple high-speed entries into water with varying surface tensions. We found that in the middle speed range, drops on cones that form during water entry play a significant role in delaying pressure buildup until the sphere fully enters water. Additionally, our findings reveal that in this speed range, factors like surface tension and drag have a minimal impact on splash peak pressure. Our research also compares our results to earlier studies in lower speed ranges and a higher speed range, known as the "splash" regime, and explains how they relate to the current regime of focus, known as the "seal" regime.

We investigate the impact of a specific type of axionic terms, which include both the non-perturbative $C_4$ self-dual four-form field term and the $G_4$ four-form field term from M-theory, within the context of $\textit{SO}(10)$ grand unified theories. The aim is to demonstrate the inevitability of electroweak symmetry breaking through these terms in a scenario where the $\textit{SU}(2)_L \times \textit{SU}(2)_R$ symmetry remains unbroken at high energies. We further examine the potential for these terms to contribute to the dark matter density and the resulting constraints on the model.

Our calculations using first-principles methods have examined the orbital occupation in cubanite, specifically the 3d energy levels of iron within two-ferric spinel structures. By breaking down the total energy width, we found that the energy ranges for each orbital are significantly dissimilar, with about 4.5eV separating the highest and lowest occupied orbitals. This large gap may contribute to stabilization of the peculiar magnetic arrangement in this compound, which features geometric frustration and long-range ordering up to quite high temperatures.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as discrete-time quantum walk, combines principles from quantum mechanics and computation to create innovative tools for searching and sorting. Research has successfully demonstrated exciton Rabi oscillations in both cadmium sulfide and selenide nanoscale layers, showcasing the potential for coupling photons with semiconductors on the microscopic level. These experiments have also revealed the importance of considering environment effects on quantum systems. A study involving cadmium sulfide nanoscale layers revealed the massive impact of external magnetic fields in creating giant Rabi oscillations between a photon and an electron pair bond called a dark exciton. The research found that even tiny variations in the dark exciton's energy could lead to enormous fluctuations in its behavior. Furthermore, by calculating the energy differences, the researchers were able to explain the unusual fluctuations observed and predicted that similar fluctuations could occur in other semiconductor nanoscale layers that support dark excitons.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D non-symmorphic wallpaper network lattice, and we've demonstrated the presence of tunable Dirac points at the high-symmetry positions within its electronic band structure. By adjusting the height parameter h, a non-symmorphic glide reflection symmetry is established at these points, leading to a quadratic reduction in energy and an in-plane electric field that can be used to shift the positions of the Dirac points. Furthermore, we found that this results in varying velocities and an oscillatory behavior in the energy of the edge states in the system's phonon spectrum. Calculations using an ab initio method based on DFT+U revealed that this lattice structure exhibits ferromagnetic properties, and we accounted for the exchange interaction's impact on the band structure using a tight-binding model.

Quantum states of multiple particles are described by the Wigner function, representing classical phases in Wigner phase space. The Wigner function's positive part defines the coherent phase space. We investigate the quantum-optical catalysis effect on an arbitrary beam, determining the conditions under which the resulting state will occupy the coherent phase space specified by a parabola in Wigner phase space. This analysis shows that a specific beam can generate a desired state, identified as a 3D Schubert curve, originating from a 2D parabolic curve when a beam interacting with a cavity is considered. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a particular state corresponding to a double parabola can be generated from an arbitrary beam through quantum-optical catalysis with single photons.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the differential properties of the Weyl tensor. As such properties determine the geometric properties of spacetime, this analysis yields the conformal structure of spacetime. We review the progress made in solving the Weyl conformal geometry equation in various contexts, from its initial formulation to its connection with the Schouten conformally invariant curvature tensor, and specifically its solution related to the Weyl curvature conjecture.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for predicting polymer structures. In this newly developed technique, a set of predefined monomers with known properties serves as input to a linear regression model that yields potential bond formations between the monomers, which are then translated into a form that can be processed by an integer programming solver to yield a possible polymer structure. A distinguishing feature of this model is the inclusion of side chains within the monomers, allowing for predictions on molecules with complex, branching structures. Evaluations of this method on datasets consisting of peptides and polymeric compounds with side chains have shown it to be a highly effective predictor of chemical compounds.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To improve the accuracy of computer-based methods, researchers often use sophisticated techniques that incorporate extensive training data and complex models. However, using these methods can lead to multiple problems, including the need for extensive computational time, significant amounts of data for training, and limited generalizability to new, unseen patients. To address these challenges, we propose a novel approach called the Dilated Dense Focus A-Unet (DDAUnet), which leverages multiple densely connected blocks to combine information and patch-based attention to focus on relevant details. By using this model, we were able to achieve significant improvements in segmentation accuracy on two publicly available datasets, the LIDC-IDRI and the CTSi. Moreover, we found that the DDAUnet model leaped above the state-of-the-art performance on these datasets, with an increase of 5.14% in the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and 10.19% in the 50% Hausdorff distance (HD50) when compared to the current top-performing method, the U-Shaped Res-Dense Unet.

Code-mixed languages combine two or more languages, such as Hindi and English, which are commonly used in social media interactions, presentations, and sporting events. Without a universally accepted definition, research has been hindered, yet it's evident that code-mixed languages are widespread in multilingual communities. This lack of a standard framework makes it difficult to develop effective methods for code-mixed text. We propose a three-part framework: first, identifying the types of code-mixed text; second, determining the language combinations; and third, classifying the code-mixed text into two categories: alternating and mixed codes. We apply this framework to commonly analyzed topics like sentiment analysis, sentiment classification, and text classification. By establishing a foundation for code-mixed NLP research, our study aims to encourage the development of uniform standards and effective methods for processing code-mixed text.

The metric that measures the similarity between a given image description and a set of reference descriptions, most notably the FC5 metric, has been widely adopted to assess the quality of neural image captioning models. Although widely used, these evaluation methods rely solely on the captions generated by the model being tested and do not account for actual human-generated captions. In fact, research has shown that these metrics often correlate with the level of caption diversity produced by the model, rather than its semantic similarity to human captions. Furthermore, the inclusion of human captions in evaluation sets has been debated, with some arguing that they are too variable to be trusted, while others see them as essential for creating more realistic captions. In this study, we examine the relationship between human-generated captions in evaluation sets and the accuracy of image captioning models, and discuss the implications for using such data in evaluation, particularly in relation to the FC5 metric.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with varying oxygen content, have garnered significant attention due to their intriguing combination of electronic properties, ranging from metallic to insulating behavior, and their potential uses in oxide electronics and interfaces. To better understand the electronic and structural features of tantalum oxide, specifically Ta$_2$O$_5$, we used theoretical calculations to examine its possible lattice structures and phases. Through a combination of ab-initio total energy calculations and evaluation of lattice dynamics, and Monte Carlo simulations in the canonical ensemble, we investigated various dimer and polymeric arrangements of Ta and O atoms. The results show that the most stable structure corresponds to a dimer model with a specific bond angle, and the energy barriers between different polymer chain configurations were identified as 1.3 eV for a dimer tilt and 0.5 eV for a dimer rotation. The theoretical findings are consistent with experimental data showing Ta atoms located at the oxygen bond angles. Additionally, we found that the dimer tilt is associated with a Peierls gap, while the dimer rotation leads to a stabilization of a Mott insulating state within a specific range of distances between dimers.

The spread of misinformation on social media has been influenced by users' online interactions, news consumption, and internet usage habits. Furthermore, the COVID-19 pandemic's onset coincided with a significant shift in Reddit users' geographic origins, likely affecting the dissemination of false information online. By analyzing the users of two popular Reddit forums, /r/news and /r/politics, our study reveals that there was a notable decline in the sharing of false news articles between March and September 2020. We found that this decrease in false news sharing was not attributed to changes in online behavior, but rather to the decline of users from the Eastern Time Zone. Notably, before the pandemic, users from the Eastern Time Zone were more likely to share false information, especially if they had a shorter online history. Our research suggests that the big geographic shift on Reddit was a key factor contributing to the reduction in false information being circulated.

Humans use spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Through listening to instructions, learners can acquire critical information about tasks and their underlying purposes. Yet, the relationship between language and actions remains complex, and numerous aspects of it remain unexplored. Primarily, the connection between the meaning of spoken words and the physical world they describe lacks a common framework. To address this, we examine the link between spoken words, actions, and their underlying intentions using a set of instructions from human teachers performing manipulation tasks. Our analysis reveals the relationship between spoken words and actions through intentional graphs, which reflect the connection between words, actions, and their underlying intentions. We also discovered a recurring pattern in which related words are linked by a common concept called a super node. Furthermore, our study measures the frequency and position of nodes in instructions, which could be valuable for future research on teaching through demonstration.

A new framework for describing conformal field theory complexity has been established in (arXiv: 2105.04470, arXiv: 2105.04472). Within this context, a set of nonlinear Euler-Arnold equations serves as a characteristic signature of complexity, whose specific form is determined by a universal, physically-prefixed parameter. This prefixed parameter manifests as a scalar value in d dimensions, which we have found to be directly linked to the proportionality constant in the fundamental complexity evolution equation. Furthermore, in the course of our earlier studies, particularly in arXiv: 2105.04472, we demonstrated that a particular class of solvable lattice operators could be effectively represented as a complex operator in a d-dimensional space, with specific properties. Here, we expand on this insight by revealing that the lattice operator's intrinsic characteristics, including its asymptotic behavior, geometric structure, and interactions, can be interpreted through the lens of conformal field theory in (1+1)D. Notably, our findings related to the Euler-Arnold equations hold universally, without dependence on the specific d-dimensional space in which the operator is defined.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems like dialog agents are at the forefront with their evolving technology. As a result, the demand for automated testing methods is growing to ensure these systems' effectiveness and efficiency. Currently, manual testing methods are the primary approach, which is time-consuming and limited in its capabilities. To keep pace with the rapid development of conversational systems, automated testing is essential. To this end, we present an automated testing framework known as DART, which leverages machine learning-based approaches to effectively assess these complex systems. DART's capabilities are demonstrated through a series of experiments conducted on a dataset comprising conversational systems extracted from publicly available data.

Cross-domain recommendation has been a highly sought-after topic in recent years, as it enables the effective utilization of abundant multi-source data. However, traditional methods are often hampered by the requirement for identical feature spaces across domains, restrictive assumption that needs further validation. In our research, we assemble a group of domains where user-item interactions are sparse, which we call the'multi-sparse-domain' setting. To tackle this novel context, we develop a Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Recommendation framework that leverages enhanced comprehensive aspect preference learning. Within this framework, a novel Multi-Sparse-Domain Assessment is conducted to identify eligible domains for collaborative information. Next, we integrate aspect-aware Graph Neural Networks and Personalized Cross-domain Learning to develop a novel Enhanced Comprehensive Aspect Preference Learning model. This model's capacity to handle multi-sparse domains is validated through extensive experiments, conducted on real-world datasets.

Hypatia is an open-source mathematical programming modeling language and solver link layer (SLL) for Julia, allowing users to efficiently create high-performance optimization models utilizing conic formulations with multiple variables, including semidefinite, affine, and generalized entropy variables, as well as quadratic, second-order, and polynomial cone constraints, among others. Conic formulations offer a versatile and expressive framework for presenting and solving complex problems from various disciplines. Due to their versatile nature, conic formulations have found applications across disciplines such as machine learning, finance, electronics, and energy management. Models created with Hypatia can be solved using Hypatia's internal solver or other compatible solvers linked through SLL, including SDPA-QD, MOSEK, GUROBI, and IPOPT.

The escalating use of artificial intelligence has necessitated careful consideration of its limitations, especially when applying learned models in new contexts. In the sensitive field of medical imaging, particularly with MRI, ensuring quality is a pressing concern, affecting not just patient safety but also diagnostic accuracy and treatment efficacy. The rise of artificial neural networks has provided a promising solution, enabling the automated detection of irregularities and problems with MRI equipment. However, as MRI facilities are numerous and disparate, with distinct operating environments, there's a growing need to ensure that such models generalise effectively across various settings. This study addresses the challenge of adapting a trained neural network to effectively generalize across new, unseen factors, employing a technique called multi-task group method for generalization. It was tested using data from 19 facilities, involving variations in equipment, technical parameters, and geographic locations. The results show that the network's performance on unfamiliar data remains above a significant baseline, demonstrating its ability to generalize across various settings. Furthermore, an examination was conducted to understand the factors that the network is able to generalize across and those it does not, also looking at the role of sample size in relation to data from specific facilities. The findings have important implications for implementing artificial neural networks in MRI quality assurance, specifically regarding data collection, effective generalization, and the impact of changes in operating environments on the validity of test data.

To understand the implications of growing private EV populations on the resilience of distribution networks, a new optimization framework is proposed that accounts for various EV charging scenarios. The proposed method uses a dual decomposition approach to solve a convex optimization problem that incorporates individual private EV owners' decisions and aggregate network impacts. A key finding is that, to ensure network stability, charging restrictions become necessary when demand outstrips supply, with the extent of this limitation dependent on specific network characteristics and local energy market configurations. Another key discovery reveals that, when charging infrastructure is widespread, differences in pricing schemes are minimal, with prices converging to a level that is just enough to cover incentives for cost-effective owners to charge, rather than a fully optimized price.

In multi-agent soccer simulations, motivation plays a key role in determining a team's success. Research has focused on refining the scoring system to replicate natural player motivation. However, little work has been done on the dynamics of motivation within the game's context. Our approach involves analyzing the sequence relationships between motivation and players' actions, then using LSTM networks to model these patterns across an entire soccer match. When tested against public data, our method showed a 20% improvement in accuracy compared to a benchmark approach. To further validate our approach, we conducted an experiment in which two teams, with distinct motivation systems, competed in a match. The results revealed that our method accurately predicted the outcome of the match and the timing of its key events.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We studied the fundamental properties of bulk GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 materials crystallizing in the AuCu3 structure. Our results match previous experimental and theoretical data on the GdSn3 compound and indicate that CmSn3 and GdSn3 both adopt a type-A anti-ferromagnetic configuration and display metallic behavior. Notably, the magnetic moment diminishes with rising Cm content in the GdxCm1-xSn3 series, and these materials share some key characteristics, rendering them promising for spintronic technology applications.

Using a model that incorporates dynamical chiral symmetry breaking, the QCD vacuum is analyzed to predict the properties of hypothetical baryons and mesons. The study focuses on mesons with odd parity, particularly the orbital, spin, and flavor components, to provide predictions for their masses and decay modes. The model also enables the calculation of masses for baryons with strange and charm quarks, as well as odd-parity baryons that have yet to be discovered, and it further extends to mesons with heavy quarks, Higgs bosons, and even axions.

The concept of root subgroups in the classical Chevalley groups over a given field has a significant implications for the structure and properties of these groups. A fundamental theorem by the mathematicians Shoji and Hagiwara establishes relationships between the conjugating operators of these root subgroups within the symmetric groups and the Coxeter groups of type B, and they prove the conjugating operators are rational functions that contain only even powers of the variable x. In this study, we provide a generalization of the mentioned theorem, discovering that the conjugating operators for the classical Chevalley groups over a field with an odd characteristic contain powers of x with a specific parity, which is determined based on the n-fold duals of a polynomial called the Frobisher invariant.

Using the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and assuming a standard cosmological model, we calculated the weak lensing convergence of Type Ia supernovae within their observed distance range. Our results show that the convergence is proportional to the optical brightness of SNe Ia with a precise gradient of 1.92 ± 0.05 mag, consistent with predictions made by the mislensing effect. We further validated this prediction using the Amo-G16 cosmological model and found the convergence's dependence on distance to be in line with the expected Conrad profile. Our study also provided the parameters for the Conrad profile in the observed distance range of SNe Ia and demonstrated that the relation between convergence and luminosity remains unaffected to a 1% level up to a certain lensing convergence threshold, which we estimated to be approximately 0.015.

We investigated T-dots in silicon photonic material to achieve efficient optical coupling and to facilitate the construction of high-speed photonic communication systems. By leveraging the fundamental principles of photonic quantum computing and silicon photonic technology, we designed a structure where T-dots serve as nodes for optical information. Our results show that a specific T-dots design, namely a 500nm diameter T-dots with a 200nm radius of curvature, exhibits an exceptionally strong focus effect with an optical field concentration factor of over 40. This phenomenon enables the precise control of light flow and minimization of data loss due to scattering. Furthermore, our findings indicate that even at high data transfer rates, as occurs in quantum simulations, the focus effect remains robust and does not deteriorate.

For our task that considers context, a relevant image region can be any part of the image, not limited to surrounding areas as seen in traditional context-based methods. We call this type of context "generalized context". We believe this type of context is crucial for deep object detectors. To support this claim, we created a custom image dataset with a focus on generalized context, specifically designed to assess the context-aware capabilities of deep object detectors. In this dataset, each training image is paired with a corresponding target image that features the same objects after a transformation such as a rotation, scaling, or flipping. We believe this dataset enables the evaluation of deep object detectors' capacity to be aware of this type of context. Notably, our results show that many popular object detectors are more adept at recognizing rotated objects than the benchmark models proposed in RBD [1, 2].

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum^k_{j=1}\|u_j\|^2\right)\Delta u_i=\frac{f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)}{|x|^\beta}+\varepsilon h_i(x)$ holds for $i=1,\ldots,k$, within the bounded domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $x$ contains the origin with smooth boundary, and for a certain condition $\beta\in [0,2)$; here $m$ denotes a function that belongs to Kirchhoff type, $f_i$ are functions that belong to $C^1(\overline{\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^k})$, and $h_i$ and $u_i$ are functions whose properties are further specified. It is further assumed that $f_i$ satisfy the Trudinger-Moser type growth condition, and that there exists a solution $(u_1,\ldots,u_k)$ for the given system of equations for any choice of small positive values for $\varepsilon$; moreover, when $\varepsilon=0$ there is an associated mountain pass whose energy can be estimated as does the energy for $f_i$ when $\beta\in [0,2)$

We investigate the concentration of the expectation of a function of random variables that follow a specific dependence structure. Given a positively weighted graph G and independent, identically distributed random variables denoted as X_u for each node u in the graph, we define a new set of random variables Y_u as the product of their corresponding X_u values, weighted by the corresponding edge weights in G. If the graph G contains no cycles, we establish an inequality showing the subgaussian concentration of sums of these producted random variables. For general graphs with no isolated nodes, we establish a more general inequality showing the subgaussian concentration of sums of these producted random variables for a specific range of weights. Both of these inequalities were previously established under more restrictive conditions in A. concentration inequalities for the sum of dependent random variables in A. and D. N. A. and D. N. also explored similar concentration inequalities in B. and D. N. with different dependence structures.

This note makes explicit the symplectic counterpart of a recent chart-based interpretation in [Cartella-Ruggeri 2021], where the contact version of Darboux's theorem was rephrased in terms of local coordinates. We demonstrate the equivalence of this formulation to the standard contact version of Darboux's theorem by utilizing the concept of contact equivalence. Additionally, the note's appendices provide a brief overview of contact equivalence and local coordinate definitions.

A key challenge in kidney exchange programs involves determining which incompatible donor-recipients pairs to include, given a vast number of registered donors willing to donate to unknown recipients. To effectively utilize this resource, it is crucial to maximize the number of transplants performed. We develop a mathematical framework to maximize the transplants by selecting the most beneficial donor-recipients pairs, considering the complexity of blood type relationships and geographic distance between donors and recipients. We demonstrate that when prioritizing multiple criteria such as compatibility, waiting time, and donor characteristics, using multi-objective optimization yields a more accurate representation of real-world situations. We also examine the feasibility of using publicly available resources, like online donor registries, by analyzing a dataset from the UK. Our study shows that, for example, with approximately 6000 listed patients and 15000 registered donors, a significant portion of transplants can be facilitated among patients waiting for kidneys from donors with a different blood type.

This paper undertakes a comprehensive mathematical examination of the word2vec model, particularly in its implementation with the Skip-gram learning method. We investigate how NLP embeddings, now widely applied, are impacted by the distribution of terms within a given corpus. A mathematical framework is developed to predict the learned representations of word2vec based on corpus characteristics. We then use this framework to analyze the N-YSE17 corpus, which was previously used to create a stock market sentiment indicator. We find that the neural network's learned representations are indeed consistent with its maximally likely corpus prediction. However, we also discover issues with the original N-YSE17 sentiment indicator, including label distribution imbalances and artifacts resulting from the embedding generation process. We propose an alternative method for creating sentiment indicators, leveraging the optimal hyperplane separation problem to achieve better results.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDEC systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming strategy in [1].
Fair-throughput and sum-throughput optimisation problems are defined and formulated.
By leveraging an algorithm similar to the one introduced in [1], we can find the optimal fair-throughput and sum-throughput values for SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM systems.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and high-resolution interface representation. This method enables a second-order conservative numerical scheme and has been effectively applied to solve various problems, including Stefan problems, dendrite growth, and Rayleigh--B\'enard instabilities, even in the presence of melting boundaries.

Our study focuses on the rational behind players' decisions in multiplayer games, specifically those with multiple agents. By assuming other players act rationally, we show that optimal strategies for others can be represented by a set of stable states, or equilibria, which can be learned using deep reinforcement learning methods. These optimal strategies are invariant to the number of other players. We achieve state-of-the-art performance on several datasets by utilizing features derived from the equilibria and multi-agent context. Notably, our approach demonstrates the significance of considering multiple agents in games by showcasing improved performance when other players are accounted for, even in the presence of noise. All code and models are publicly accessible.

An analysis of a stochastic model is presented, where a virus spreads through a network of interconnected individuals, and infected individuals form new connections with uninfected individuals in a preventive manner. The model involves a dynamic change in network dynamics and an immune response, and we derive exact expressions for the probability of an individual becoming infected, as well as an approximate expression for the rate of network changes, using a birth-death process as a benchmark. Through numerical simulations, we verify the accuracy of our analytical predictions, and demonstrate that a simple adaptive immunity response can lead to the exclusion of a pathogen from a network, even in the presence of permanent connections between network members.

Our proposed framework simplifies the complex relationships between datasets, theoretical predictions, and parton distribution functions (PDFs) by treating PDFs as variables influencing theoretical predictions, rather than targets. This shift in perspective allows us to treat PDFs as variables that need to be adjusted to match measured data, a approach identical to the traditional method of fitting PDFs to data. Our framework maintains the same level of information as the original formulation and is thus fully equivalent. However, this new perspective offers several practical benefits, including the practicality of treating PDFs at different energies as variables in data fitting, and the potential to develop novel algorithms for fitting PDFs.

To enhance the effectiveness of experience replay for policy optimization, we introduce a technique called variance diminution based experience replay. This method leverages a critical property of the advantage function to reduce the impact of irregular returns, resulting in a more uniform distribution of advantages in the replay buffer. Furthermore, we derive a theoretical bound on the variance of the advantage function, which serves as a key ingredient in developing an efficient algorithm for scaling experience replay. Specifically, we propose a simple yet efficient algorithm, VDBER, which utilizes a targeted batch size to reduce the variance of the advantage function to a desired level. We provide a theoretical guarantee for the optimal batch size and demonstrate the superiority of VDBER over standard experience replay methods.

In our analysis of conversational dialogue, we face numerous possible responses 
to any given history, leading us to present the MultiTalk Dataset. This large 
dataset comprises over 320,000 written conversational dialogue sentences, 
maintaining a high degree of complexity (a 10-way branching factor) along with 
6 conversation turns through strategically chosen continuation branches. Our study 
of dialogue generation involves multiple advancements, particularly in highly 
branching scenarios. To evaluate the diversity of generated text, we introduce a 
simple scoring algorithm grounded in bipartite graph matching, effectively 
incorporating various references. Our research spans multiple text generation 
tasks at various levels of conversational depth, utilizing text features derived 
automatically from pre-trained models. Ultimately, our primary challenge is a 
complex theory of mind problem that necessitates controlled text generation 
based on anticipated listener reactions.

We introduce a novel computational approach that leverages an existing suite of $N$-body codes to efficiently create comprehensive simulations for a specific class of cosmological models, thereby circumventing the need for a separate development of an $N$-body solver. This method allows us to rapidly generate high-precision simulations for a broad range of cosmological parameters. Our primary focus is on developing an $N$-body solver for the conformal coupling model of gravity, which we then apply to a representative set of simulations featuring a $1024^3$ grid and an initial displacement of $\Delta x = 1.0 h^{-1}{\rm kpc}$. Our findings show that using $\xi = 0.25$ yields the most accurate results for the clustering spectrum and the matter power spectrum. We also found that the value of $\xi$ has a minimal impact on the evolution of the large-scale structure for $k < 1 h^{-1}{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. Furthermore, our simulations adhere to the observed relationship between the amplitude of gravitational waves and the rate of cosmic acceleration.

We investigate the relationship between Gaussian free fields and multiple Schramm-Loewner evolution, specifically on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ with real boundary, and extend previous work by Chandra-Duplantier-Rhodes-VDH and Kupiainen-Rhodes-VDH to multiple SLE driven by general GUE compacts on the real line. The connection between GFF and multiple SLE is reflected in the formula for the average total length, as well as the number and size distribution of SLE's target curve's self-intersections. Moreover, we establish that for $\gamma<1$, multiple SLE with $\kappa\in(0,4)$ and $\Delta\in(1,4)$ driven by a random log-gas with discrete spectrum has a phase transition at $\kappa=4$ within the model's parameter space, with distinct behavior for $\kappa<4$ including the existence of power law decay for loop heights. This indicates that multiple SLE with interaction driven by the Dyson model also has a phase transition at $\Delta=4$ within the model's parameter space.

MediaWiki's 'WorkingWiki' is an open-source, open-architecture collaborative research environment built on top of the Wikipedia editing platform. Developed in response to the limitations of current data sharing methods, WorkingWiki enables secure, controlled communities to safely collaborate and analyze sensitive data within the system. It integrates multiple features, including customizable interfaces, a module for managing and analyzing data, and secure user management. WorkingWiki's modular design allows users to easily integrate additional features and functions via plug-and-play components called'services.' As an illustration of WorkingWiki's capabilities in action, it has been applied to the analysis of multiple lines of code related to the LHCb experiment.

We examined a highly reactive methane-air jet flame in a crossflow, which was subjected to different flow conditions including a curved surface and surface turbulence with various intensities. The flame was unstable in its natural state but became steady when acoustic forcing was applied to it. Based on these observations, a linear model was developed to understand the dynamics of this flame. The model, which includes a detailed chemical reaction model, successfully replicated the results of the non-linear simulations even when the acoustic forcing was altered. A key finding was that flame instability in the natural state was caused by Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities resulting from the interaction between the flame surface and turbulent flow rather than hydrodynamic instabilities within the flame.

We investigate the impact of neutrinos interacting with ultralight dark matter on the $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay and cosmological parameters. Assuming that neutrinos have a non-zero mass and that the dark matter is ultralight with a mass similar to the neutrino mass, we consider interactions mediated by a light vector boson with conserved charge. By analyzing four scenarios of neutrino mass hierarchies, we determine the minimal dark matter density required to accommodate the heaviest neutrino mass within the Arbesbach et al. limit. Consequently, this limit is strengthened to $|g_{\rm A}^{\rm V}/g_{\rm A}^{\rm S}| \lesssim 10^{-3}$ for a vector boson with a mass in the $10^{-25}$eV range. Furthermore, we find that the dark matter density is directly proportional to the square of the light vector boson mass, and its impact on the $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay is modified to be in line with the nuclear matrix element. Additionally, we determine the dark matter density constraints from the CMB and large-scale structure data within the effective field theory framework, which are in agreement with previous findings.

We introduce a nonlocal gravity theory, expanding the Einstein tensor in a series of increasing complexity within a frame-based formulation, leveraging the concept of "naturalness". By comparing the Einstein tensor to a generic second-order tensor, we determine its nonlocal equivalent using the trace relationship. A constitutive relation for the nonlocal gravity framework is then derived, leading to the nonlocal Einstein equation in a frame-independent form. By applying the Euler-Lagrange formalism, we alternatively obtain the nonlocal Einstein equation through variational derivatives. Both approaches yield the same result, confirming the nonlocal Einstein equation within the Euler-Lagrange formulation.

Our analysis combines 18 datasets from recent genome-wide association studies with expression and chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing data from multiple tissues. This integration uncovers novel associations with a high degree of consistency across tissues, with the majority being cell-type specific. Notably, we find that while the number of significant associations within each tissue is comparable, certain regions are associated with multiple traits in different tissues. Furthermore, regions associated with a particular trait in a specific cell type are generally found in high numbers in that cell type, with some exceptions. We observe a relationship between the number of associated regions and heritability explanations for these 18 traits.

The introduction discusses the significance of understanding QCD dynamics, especially in high-energy collisions, where multiple partons participate in scattering processes. As a result, there has been a surge in experimental data requiring accurate predictions, with some indicating discrepancies. To address this, a review is conducted of available theoretical predictions for three types of scattering processes: deep inelastic scattering, proton-proton collisions, and heavy ion collisions. Specifically, it examines predictions involving the collapse of color fields, as well as predictions for specific observables such as multiplicity, charged hadron distributions, and flow patterns. A key finding is that, while there are variations in predictions, they remain within the range of experimental uncertainty, with some exceptions in heavy ion collisions that may indicate interplay between partons and the medium.

Observations indicate that some X-ray binaries in the Galaxy's center remain inactive for decades.  The time between outbursts in other similar binaries can be found using power law distributions, which imply that the longest intervals contain a significant fraction of missing binaries, thus potentially distorting measurements of outburst periods.  A new analysis using cumulative distribution functions confirms previous results showing that the time between outbursts in the binaries RX J13103-4532 and X7 for example follows a power law with indices 24 and 16 respectively.  Furthermore, the analysis provides constraints on the number of binaries for which the longest recurrence intervals are greater than a certain value, exceeding 10 times the largest observed interval.  This information can be used to model the outburst patterns in the Galaxy's center, specifically for the binaries 1E 03 50 and G359.561-0.089, which have observed intervals of 76-495 years, and 76-587 years for the G359.561-0.089 binary is considered too large given the current data set.

THz-driven atomic vibrations in solids result in the interaction of spins and
electrons with sound, a concept proved by experiments but whose underlying
mechanism remains unknown. Utilizing an exact solution to a one-dimensional
Sêgèe model, we uncover the intricate dynamics of spin and electron interaction
with sound, demonstrating that these interactions change depending on the
direction of the lattice displacement. As a direct consequence, we find that
the magnitude of electron-phonon and spin-ornon interactions varies with
speed as well as a change in their type (e.g., from a form that slows down to
a form that speeds up), a phenomenon predicted to affect critical temperatures
and lattice vibration-induced anomalies in materials. Our study is relevant to
a wide range of materials, including one-dimensional materials, copper oxides,
and nitrides, and semiconductor and carbon-based materials.

Humans who engage in conversation with each other on a semantic level typically exploit various linguistic varieties to their advantage. They may employ different tones, ask questions, offer excuses, make apologies, express gratitude, convey sympathy, cite sources, tell stories, provide definitions, offer suggestions, offer facts, offer opinions, and more. Yet, when presented with a statement, they rarely respond with a straightforward "yes" or "no." Rather, their responses often take the form of a related statement, a question, or another type of utterance that deviates from the original query. We examine the diversity of semantic varieties in conversations by drawing on natural language processing techniques and a vast corpus of text. Our analysis reveals the most prevalent semantic varieties, their evolutionary patterns over time, the contexts in which they appear, as well as the most commonly encountered response types in conversations. We also introduce a new challenge focused on selecting the most appropriate semantic variety from a range of options to use in a given conversation, along with associated evaluation metrics and a comprehensive dataset consisting of annotated text.

The occurrence of rotating surface convective hydrogen burning stars with masses below 0.25 solar masses remains poorly understood due to the limited number of observable low-mass stars in our galaxy. Convective hydrogen burning stars in this mass range exhibit differential rotation, which can influence their morphology and rotation rates. Using numerical methods, we simulated the rotation rates of low-mass stars by solving the equations for hydrodynamic stability, nuclear reaction rates, and radiative transport within their interiors. We tested various numerical methods for accuracy and efficiency and developed an iterative approach to solve the nonlinear equations. We then mapped the parameter space for low-mass stars by simulating and analyzing their internal dynamics for various rotation rates. We found that the limits of stable rotation are marked by the inner border of a nonlinear instability, which directly influences a star's moment of inertia and angular momentum. As a result, we obtained equations defining these limits, which can be compared to theoretical predictions made by other researchers. Furthermore, we found that the moment of inertia and angular momentum of low-mass stars can be accurately predicted using simple power-law models. By examining the effects of magnetic field, surface convective behavior, and inner boundary conditions on their rotation rates, we identified several factors influencing the limits of stable rotation. We also analyzed the effects of differential rotation, shear mixing, and magnetic field on their rotation rates and identified several possible indicators for future observational verification.

For complex processes with multiple objects produced in hadron collisions,
amplitude analyses are a powerful tool to study anomalous couplings.
However, the vast number of possible reactions, events, and kinematic
configurations with multiple objects necessitates a comprehensive approach
to handle experimental data. In this work, a general framework is presented
for amplitude analyses to incorporate various sources of data inhomogeneity
and to provide reliable and universally applicable results. The proposed method
is demonstrated by analyzing data from $W$ boson production in proton-proton
collisions.

A new model based on a comprehensive expression of radiation energies has been proposed, and it effectively elucidates the development of external shock radiation in GRBs. This model enamel also enables the calculation of various observable parameters through a set of standardized equations. It can be applied across a broad spectrum of observers and can be further refined based on empirical observations. Furthermore, this model can be compared to other proposed models, such as those by Panaitescu, by examining changes in index values.

Bipartite graphs depicting connections between distinct groups of objects have numerous practical applications, and their visualization often takes the form of a 2-tier layout where corresponding entities are aligned horizontally across two parallel lines, connected by lines representing relationships between them. The task of splitting these graphs to improve readability by reducing overlap and staircases has been found to be computationally expensive for large scales. In response, we have developed an algorithmic approach that utilizes a neighborhood search technique and constraints to break connections, and either merges or splits connected components based on an analysis of their structure. We have also established a performance guarantee for our method, demonstrating that the number of splits required to achieve a desirable level of readability is proportional to the size of a relevant parameter, thereby providing a framework for further efficiency gains when problems are complex but solvable.

Bipedal robots are prone to fluctuations in stability during locomotion resulting from complex interactions between ground contact points, Consequentially, leading to control and balance management challenges. To overcome these issues, researchers have been exploring the use of multiple thrusters in robotic legs. Although less common, this type of propulsion offers significant advantages, including enhanced efficiency, reduced energy expenditure, and improved stability through torque and acceleration manipulation. This paper presents a thruster-supported bipedal locomotion concept, demonstrating the potential benefits of this design in achieving faster speed and enhanced stability through oscillatory gait patterns. A robust feedback control design is developed and validated through simulations and physical experiments, showing the feasibility of the proposed approach.

We define a property in valued domains called being "totally residue" which occurs when the map sending each principal prime to its generic residue acts on primes rather than just prime divisors. For domains with a field characteristic not two, being totally residue is equivalent to being quasicohenoidal, a property previously established in equal characteristic two contexts.

In order to counter energy efficiency challenges and security threats resulting from complex deep learning models' increased size, we propose a novel technique called HyperDegrade.  This technique involves training a set of significantly smaller models in different task domains and aggregating their outputs through weighted sum encoding, thereby achieving significant gains in model size, computational expense, and memory consumption without compromising performance.  Our research shows that models reduced to 2% of their original size still maintain comparable functionality to their full-scale counterparts, while also significantly decreasing their attack surfaces and reducing computational expenses by up to 6 times with minimal top-level application effects.

We introduce a novel chord diagram coefficient, the n-fold disentangling operator, which systematically produces operators that identify and distinguish links with distinct classical or welded knot properties. This operator can be viewed as a variation of the Kauffman bracket skein relation, and its applications are demonstrated within the classical and welded knot theories.
We've demonstrated that combining the Fox-Hatcher loop with a specific 2-cocycle yields a distinct Vassiliev invariant of order three, which hasn't been previously described in the literature.

In cooperative systems with multiple tasks, and given the constraints of time and resources, it's not always beneficial to carry out tasks and communicate with each other at the same time. In fact, research has shown that sometimes it's best to delay both completely, until a synchronized moment. This phenomenon is known as the "curse of cooperation" and it can be addressed through optimization problems that consider the synchronization of tasks with deadlines. In this paper, we take it a step further and explore how to optimize the synchronization of tasks with deadlines in a more complex setting, with multiple tasks that need to be carried out by different robots that communicate with each other. We consider a network of robots that can move and carry out tasks in different locations, and that need to synchronize their tasks with deadlines while moving within the network. We show that even in this more complex setting, it's possible to find optimized solutions by formulating optimization problems that consider the synchronization of tasks with deadlines. Additionally, we provide a method for finding a solution that is close to the optimal one, by using a simulated annealing algorithm. We test this method with simulations that involve different scenarios of robots and tasks with deadlines, and we compare it to other methods that are available in literature.

This paper exposes the practical privacy risks associated with the use of sensitive user data in vertical federated learning, specifically in regards to user privacy and data safety. We examine the potential consequences of a malicious model developer exploiting private model updates for financial gain, theft of valuable information, or reputational damage resulting from the public disclosure of sensitive user data. We outline the technical details of several privacy assaults, including a scheme for recovering individual images from aggregate model updates in a horizontally distributed learning setting that can also be applied to vertical learning, as well as methods for extracting and manipulating individual data points from aggregated model updates. We discuss the practical implications and possible mitigation strategies. Our findings highlight the importance of selecting trustworthy model development collaborators and implementing additional privacy protections through techniques like federated learning with federated aggregation and federated aggregation with differential privacy.

Kernel methods have proven highly effective in various machine learning applications, yet scaling them to large datasets is impractical due to the computationally expensive nature of matrix operations. To overcome this limitation, Random Fourier Features were proposed to approximate kernel functions using randomized transformations, thereby enabling the use of kernel methods on large datasets. While this method has been widely adopted, research has been focused on improving its accuracy by leveraging metadata from specific datasets. This study introduces an accurate and efficient method for estimating kernel functions using data-dependent techniques and demonstrates its efficacy through comprehensive experiments covering multiple datasets and various machine learning applications.

In our study, we demonstrated how a group that operates on a set in a recurring manner can also function on multiple subsets of that same set. Under these conditions, our findings reveal that there is a corresponding set of functions that are in turn operated upon by the same group in a similar, recurring manner – specifically within the framework of a wreath product – albeit in a more complex, multi-subset structure.

We investigate the properties of conformally flat hypersurfaces in $ \mathbb{S}^{n+1} $ with constant M\"obius curvature. It is demonstrated that these surfaces can be expressed in a specific parametric form, following the introduction of an appropriate change of coordinates. The computation of the M\"obius curvature and its conservation are key outcomes arising from this representation. Additionally, we find that closed surfaces with the same M\"obius invariant as $ \mathbb{S}^{n} $ can be parameterized by means of a specific type of catenoid in the hyperbolic space, $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$.

A new method is proposed to manage wireless resources in multi-service wireless networks that use simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). The suggested approach, based on efficient resource distribution (ERD) policy, aims to balance the need for fast data transfer with the need to conserve energy for various services with distinct requirements. To achieve this balance, the ERD policy assigns the ideal amount of bandwidth and power for each service, thereby ensuring that all services operate within their optimal operating zones. To find the ideal settings, the ERD policy uses feedback from the services to determine the current operating points for all services and then applies threshold-based linear feedback control to adjust the settings based on whether each service is near the edge of failure or not. Through simulation, it is shown that the ERD policy maintains the stability of the services, keeps them within their optimal operating zones, and boosts the overall system performance by converting unused power into available bandwidth.

Network vulnerability assessment is crucial for creating strategies to prevent the spread of malicious information and diseases in networks. Researchers often study network immunization, but traditional approaches typically focus on broad measures, such as network criticality and component size. In contrast, this paper delves into a micro-level analysis, where the removal of individual nodes during an attack is examined in detail. Based on a analysis of a network attack that removes nodes in proportion to their degree, the distribution of avalanche magnitude is calculated for a Cayley tree network.

The detection capabilities of advanced gravitational wave detectors are hindered in the high-frequency range by the quantum limitations of their reference lights. Overcoming this constraint is critical for identifying gravitational waves generated by binary neutron star mergers. To achieve this, we propose a novel interferometer configuration known as the "sloshing-Sagnac interferometer," which incorporates a rotating light cavity holding a fluctuating amount of light within its cavity. By utilizing a Michelson sensor located at the cavity's ends, this design converts the motion-induced changes in the refractive index on the light path into gravitational wave signals. Through numerical modeling, we found that the Advanced LIGO version and the proposed LIGO+ variants can achieve twice the sensitivity in the 20-50 Hz frequency range compared to the standard LIGO configuration.

Recent large-scale MIMO systems employing advanced access protocols like eXtra-Large MIMO Random Access Protocol have shown significant potential in achieving high data rates with low collision risk. To study the impact of MIMO dimensions on the spatial distribution of visibility regions in XL-MIMO RAP, we leveraged tools from stochastic geometry and queueing theory. Our analysis revealed that the number of visible base stations follows a truncated Poisson distribution, with the threshold determined by the angle between stations and their antipodal groups. Our findings leda us to further examine the statistics of visible base stations within a given visibility region, with results including the expected number of visible stations, the probability of a station being visible to another, and the variance of the number of visible stations. We also explored the impact of varying the MIMO dimension on these statistics.

Recent observations at sub-millimeter/millimeter wavelengths have revealed that the morphological structure of young stars' surrounding disks comprise various shapes, including symmetrical patterns and features resembling spiral arms, and localized phenomena like forked shapes and ridges. Theoretical models propose that the vertical shear instability (VSI) can give rise to the observed patterns in disks. We examined the effect of VSI on disks made up of multiple components and with varying outer rim temperatures. We considered three scenarios where the VSI is mildly, moderately, and extremely active and compared the predicted patterns to actual observed data, specifically looking at the Spitzer from Heritage Archive and ALMA observations of the HD 163296 and TW Hya. We analyzed the predicted features and their signal-to-noise ratios in both linear polarization and continuum emission at 870 microns. We found that the VSI produces patterns that resemble spiral arms and local variations in density, along with areas of enhanced accretion that match the locations of certain stars within the system. We also found that the VSI patterns vary over time and are rooted in the properties of the stars and their surrounding environments. We further explored the effect of the VSI on gaps within the disks and found that it can produce patterns similar to the observed phenomena around the stars HD 179721 and Vega.

The "Big Apple parameter", a novel quantity derived from the ratio of neutron skin thickness to charge radius in Sn isotopes, is used to investigate the neutron-proton ratio in these isotopes. Through a an analytical approach, the ratio is expressed in terms of nuclear density, volume, and the parameter itself. By applying the parameter to finite nuclei and neutron stars within the framework of relativistic mean-field theory, we found that the predicted neutron star radius lies within the range of 14.6 to 15.5 km. Furthermore, the ratio of neutron star to proton density at the surface falls between 0.43 and 0.47. In Sn isotopes, the Big Apple parameter is correlated with density-driven volume oscillations, neutron-proton ratio oscillations, and the neutron skin thickness, providing physical explanations for its magnitude and sensitivity to charge symmetry breaking.

Our investigation centers around a hypothesized compound, CaAg$_2$Si, whose crystallographic structure is predicted to be highly similar to that of graphene, yet it possesses an exceptionally high correlation strength. Through calculations, we have anticipated its electronic properties, particularly in a highly interacting state, where electron interactions are presumed to be quite pronounced. Our predicted properties include unusual magnetism, various phases in tensioned states, and the emergence of topological properties along certain directions. These outcomes are derived from a combination of experimental data, lattice parameters, and density functional theory, and the highly interacting state is further understood through calculations that account for electron interactions.

Researchers explored the capabilities of the NA62 experiment at CERN to enhance restrictions on a specific parameter in the Standard Model, specifically related to the interaction between a particular lepton and heavy neutral particles. By analyzing the process of $K^+ \to \pi^0 e^+ N$, they determined the present limit can be set at $2\times 10^{-6}$ for a particular lepton interaction with masses ranging from 125 to 144 MeV, a region that current production methods cannot achieve. To achieve this limit, they found that a beam target scanner with two detectors would be necessary, with optimal results using the existing NA62 setup with some upgrades, with 10^3 more recorded events in the heavy neutral lepton mass range than the current limit.

The inherent difficulty of training neural language models is addressed using a combination of both neural networks and traditional N-gram models. Our research involves training a neural language model on a subset of the data and combining it with a traditional N-gram model trained on the full data set to create a more comprehensive model. This new model incorporates the complexity of neural networks and the efficiency of N-gram models. We refer to this model as the neural N-gram model. Our experiments using the Switchboard and IARPA Babel data sets demonstrate improved results for the target language models when compared to standard N-gram models. Furthermore, the models exhibited comparable performance for the source language models.

Reconstructing three-dimensional faces in complex real-world scenarios poses significant difficulties due to frequently missing or inaccurate facial landmarks caused by various occlusions, deformations, and imaging distortions. To address this challenge, we develop a novel framework called SADRNet, which leverages a dual-face regression architecture that produces two face maps used for subsequent fusion. The fusion process employs a self-alignment technique to ensure seamless integration, even when the input face contains significant distractions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by incorporating it into a robust 3D face alignment and reconstruction framework, resulting in the optimization problem's hessian matrix being continuously updated throughout the learning process. We evaluate SADRNet on the large-scale Reg3D dataset, achieving superior results compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

Cosmological perturbations within the inflationary model, particularly those falling outside the well-behaved regime, may result in the formation of black holes of primordial origin. This research focuses on examining the relationship between these fluctuations and black hole formation within three types of $\alpha$-attractor inflation models, analyzing the connection between the initial conditions and black hole formation for perturbations with an initial growing or oscillatory phase. For perturbations initially growing, we found that black hole formation is unlikely, whereas for those that oscillate before growing, black hole formation is more probable, especially for certain modes of perturbation. This indicates that the likelihood of black hole formation is linked to the endpoint of the growing phase, particularly its location within the complex plane, compared to the endpoint of the oscillatory phase and its relation to the gravitational wave spectrum. Furthermore, we determined that black hole formation could result in the growth of perturbations that initially present a kink within the growing phase, particularly for certain $\alpha$-attractor models where the perturbation curve exhibits a sudden shift in slope.

Researchers examined marked ordered trees with the function $f(n)$ representing the number of deepest vertices, and they obtained $f(n)$ equal to $cn$ with $c$ approximately 1.736, using an unbiased random walk simulation through $f(n)$ for $n$ ranging from 1 to 10,000. Additionally, they found the probability distribution of the deepest vertex, as well as the expected time until the deepest vertex is visited for the first time, which is approximately $2n$ with a small margin of error.

This project demonstrates the capabilities of Informed OCR (iOCR) in accurately
extracting numerical data from scanned documents, using a sample dataset of
election ballot tallies. iOCR leverages a two-step approach to enhance the
quality of OCR output, beginning with a pre-processing phase that corrects
layout and font issues and continuing with a post-processing phase that
informs and corrects OCR predictions based on input data and document layout. 
The results show that iOCR outperforms standard OCR and OCR enhancement 
techniques alone, with a 20% reduction in errors and 12% improvement in 
precision. Furthermore, iOCR is cost-effective as it uses existing machine 
learning models without the need for additional training.

In linear regression models, particularly those with time series data, we have found that models exhibiting no functional redundancy can achieve optimal performance through simple regularization techniques, even when models include unnecessary features. Contrary to the common assumption that models require constraints to avoid overfitting, our research demonstrates that in the presence of no functional redundancy and given certain data conditions, models can actually become too constrained, resulting in optimal models being those with the maximum number of parameters.

A model exploring decentralized energy trading has been proposed which takes into account individual risk aversion and storage capabilities of participants. The model enables the derivation of efficient allocation strategies across various risk levels. By drawing on duality theory and particularly the dual representation of convex risks, the model's feasibility and optimality algorithms have been explicitly defined.
